name: After § 4
title: REPORT on the proposal for a decision of the European Parliament and of the Council on the mobilisation of the European Union Solidarity Fund to provide assistance to Spain regarding the floods in the Valencia Region of Spain in October 2024 and France following the damages caused by cyclone Chido in Mayotte in December 2024 and cyclone Garance in Réunion in February 2025
part_text: 4a. Notes that in the cases of La Réunion and Mayotte, the disasters identified by the Union as “regional disasters” gave rise to European aid under the Solidarity Fund (EUSF) amounting to 2,5 % of the total direct damage, and that in the case of Valencia, the disaster identified as a “major disaster” gave rise to 5,23 % of the total direct damage; observes that these aid rates are negligible given the scale of the challenges, as the total EUSF assistance for these three disasters barely exceeds EUR 1 billion, while the direct damages amount to over EUR 22 billion; points out that the weakness of those aid amounts is striking, especially considering the ease with which the Union simultaneously finds resources to assist non-member countries under the Neighbourhood Instrument, humanitarian aid, or other tailor-made special instruments, thereby giving citizens of the Union the absurd impression that the Union prefers to help others before helping its own, despite an already constrained budgetary context;
